texts.text: A small nail stands out among the vials and containers of various makeup products.
Meursault took the small nail.
Might we rest our steps awhile?
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: <You want to talk about how everyone's grown as weak as they were immediately after they entered into a contract with me, right?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I see that it hasn't escaped your notice as well, Manager.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: <I'm sure it's nothing to worry about. This is likely not a permanent phenomenon, anyway. Right, Faust?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Correct.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Indeed, Entering Sisyphe through indirect means, such as the Suicide Vending Machine, does not change the fact that we have entered another state of existence as "customers" of the department store. Ergo, our bodies as we perceive them in the phenomenal sense must have been reconstructed according to the rules of this place, which involves the Shadowed and the Symbolic—
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: H-hold on!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: So you're basically sayin' that this place is to blame for making us weaker, and we're gonna get back to normal once we're out, am I right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... Correct.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: Hmm~ Then rather than waiting for more explanation or brainstorming for ways to get stronger...
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Best we find Meur and get out of this place, chop-chop.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Happy to have a consensus for once. Our highest priority at the moment is locating Meursault; we best table any intelligence pertaining to this phenomenon until that primary objective is accomplished.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: And if we run into fights? Any plans for that?
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: <Not to worry. I don't think they can perceive us very well without Meursault, anyway.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: She's gone.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Should we... keep movin' for now? Straight ahead?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Executive Manager. I recommend returning to the restroom to regroup and reorganize.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: I... assent to Young Rodya's counsel. Let us set forth with all haste, forsooth...
texts.speaker: Don Quixote

texts.text: <No one's injured, right? I think we'll have time to reorganize later.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Let's keep going, like Rodya suggested.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ryōshū came up to me as we were preparing to proceed.
That woman knows, too.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: <So you remember too, huh? Everything that happened here—they weren't just a dream or an illusion. We were—>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: —rewound? Yes. But whatever happened didn't distort or twist the flow of time. It felt closer to... discarding time.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: Tsk. Feels like shit.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: <Well, glad to hear that I'm not the only Sinner who remembers all that, at least.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: *puff* Then here's something that'll disappoint you, C.H.: I don't remember anything.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: <You don't...?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I've only noticed the cross-sections of the memories that were severed away. *puff* It's different from having the memories like you.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: I can tell you this, though—your confusion isn't all in your head. Something happened, and we all experienced it. That's for certain.
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: <... Right.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Thanks, that's enough assurance for me.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Heh...
texts.speaker: Ryōshū

texts.text: What? Finally decided to show me to the restroom?
texts.speaker: Kromer

texts.text: Got any empty bottles left? A spare palm would do, too.
texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer

texts.text: I... don't think we have any empty bottles or... spare palms... Sorry... ha... ha...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Damn. I don't have enough eyeballs for this season's new collection...
texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer

texts.text: The customer gnaws anxiously at their fingernails.
Thank goodness I booked my dermal perm before the trend died! Once they layer the curl into every ridge of my skin, nobody will be able to tear their eyes away from me!
texts.speaker: Treatment Customer

texts.text: Strangers—stop checking me out. I'm halfway through my makeover treatment. You couldn't tell who I was even if you tried.
texts.speaker: Treatment Customer

texts.text: *sigh* This is why I hate coming down here. I suppose it can't be helped—the first floor is the only place that provides the service...
texts.speaker: Treatment Customer

texts.text: Stop staring at me!
texts.speaker: Treatment Customer

texts.text: This trend had better die soon. I don't have a single patch of bare skin left for another polka dot.
texts.speaker: Eye-shopping Customer

texts.text: A pile of unrecognizably mangled bodies that fell from one of the upper floors.
A scattered group of Le Kaki are busily scouring through the gore, pocketing what Golden Hide dregs and eyeballs they can get their hands on.
<S-so... Were you able to find them?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: They're gone... And I don't mean that like we lost one or two people—everyone except us vanished into thin air.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: C-come on~ Joke's over, everybody, come on out... Th-this isn't funny!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <... I'm not sure what the issue is on their side, but I don't think it's anything to panic about.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Oh! Right! Dante can see where everyone is. All right, where are the others?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <... They're in the restroom. Looks like they're trying all sorts of things to leave, but... not with much success.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: They wouldn't have doubled back just to loaf around in a situation like this. Maybe there's some rule or phenomenon peculiar to this place that dragged them all back to the restroom?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Let's go find Meursault first. The restroom issue can... probably wait a little longer.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: …Hm?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Hang on. Where'd everyone go?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Maybe they fell behind? I mean, the path here got pretty twisty, so...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... That might be the case. Let me go check.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Don't trouble yourself, Ishmael.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Everyone's back in the restroom—I checked. They wouldn't have doubled back just to loaf around in a situation like this, so I assume there's some rule or phenomenon peculiar to this place that dragged them all back in there.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Aha... Well, if that's the case, I'm sure we can catch up with them once we're back in the restroom.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Yeah. Our first priority is reuniting with Meursault.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <There you are, Meursault! I knew you'd be here.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I am.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What the heck, Meur! Ya could at least pretend to be surprised to see us. We came to save ya!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I quietly communicated in a way that only Meursault could hear.
<Meursault, do you...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... remember everything?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Yes. I remember every event following my entry to the Grand Magasin Sisyphe, including the events on the second floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <I don't think the other Sinners do, though.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I have heard that the Grand Magasin periodically conducts a reset of its stock, internally designated "Liquidation."
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Right... A "reset"...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Okay, so now that we have a second chance... Do you think, if we were to make different choices this time around, we could secure the Golden Bough and escape the Grand Magasin?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: There is no way to know that at the present.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: However, some things have carried over through the Liquidation.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Like what?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Every item we have purchased from the shops on each floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <The eyeballs, too? Good. At least we have that.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: And... this as well, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: With his usual, stoic cadence, Meursault produced a piece of torn flesh. It was wreathed in a golden glow.
<Kinda looks like...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... a piece of that thing the Rouges created in the Luxury Hall. That must be where it's from.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: It is likely a vestige of what emerged when we tore through what they called "the Cradle."
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <... Um, it's faint, but I think it's beating. Like a heart...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Hey, hey! Whatcha two gossiping about over there?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <N-no, we weren't gossiping. We were just... having a very normal reunion, y'know?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Right, Meursault? Aw, you have no idea how glad I am to see you again!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Correct.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: We'd better keep this on the down low from the Sinners for now, at least until I can put this troubling hunch to rest. Thankfully, Meursault seems to have picked up on my reluctance to share.
Who are you people?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Back off. I found this material first. Finders keepers. It belongs to our store now.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: "Material"...? Um... Look, this dude is our... uh, "colleague." Can we have him back, please?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: "Colleague"... Hm. I've heard that word before. Is it a brand name?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Uh...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: From what we've seen of this place so far... I don't know if common sense is all that reliable in here.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: When you said he belongs to your store... does that mean you're gonna put him to work?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: No. We have more than enough staff for this shop. It's the material that's in shortage.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Material...? Oh, okay. I suppose you wanna, uh... borrow Meursault's uniform, then...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You strangers are impossible to communicate with. I'm at my wits' end here...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: The employee gave us an exasperated look.
I said we're in a shortage of material. Material. What's so hard to understand about that?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Didn't you hear the announcement just now? The trend has changed again. A few seasons from now, there will be another thing that becomes the new trend. That's why we—and this shop—will always be in need of more material!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: I get that, I get that, but what the hell does that have to do with—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Meursault, let's get this over with.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <No point in doing this whole song and dance all over again.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We will conduct services of equivalent value to the fabric I would offer. In return for the services rendered, you will release me.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Services, huh?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: The task of helping the out-of-fashion Mannequins to the exit should provide sufficient value.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: In addition, I request a temporary release from your custody to accompany these individuals. These gauntlets in my possession will be effective in helping the Mannequins to the exit.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: That's... that's fair. We really need to get that over with, anyway.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Fine, I'll take that deal. Three should be enough.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: ... The hell's a Mannequin? And what does "helping them to the exit" even mean...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Mannequins are what they call Distortions in here, and "helping them to the exit" means "defeating them." ... I think.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Dante, did I miss a pamphlet or something?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <... Maybe?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I will take the lead.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Guys, we have Meursault now. Why don't we just split and never come back?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <I don't think we can solve this problem by just running away, Rodya.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Uh... why not? I'm a good runner.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Fleeing would not prevent me from being placed in storage.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Hm...? But you're out of "storage" now, aren'tcha?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Maybe this place has its own Laws—just like the Great Lake.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: *sigh* Let's do as Meursault says. I don't know why or how, but he seems to be well-acquainted with the department store.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <For now... let's head to where the Mannequins are.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Okay, then... we'll help them to the exit.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Good choice. You only need to help three Mannequins to the exit.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Can't wait around all day. Hurry up and make up your mind.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Well? Have you given it some thought?
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Giving the clerk what they need is probably best if you require my service, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Since you're already on the job... hurry up, will you? This season could end any minute...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: So you managed to help them to the exit. Thanks to you, more customers can now access our shop.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Whew... We've got so much on our plates at the moment. We need to redesign and revamp the entire lineup, what with the trend changing.
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: Shame we're forced to part with this material, but that's that...
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <color=#916e46>Your attention, please. The Houndstooth Season has officially ended. We are pleased to inform you that...</color>
Good grief! The trend changed again while I was wasting time shooting the breeze with you. Scram if you're not buying anything!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: So... you're not hurt anywhere, are you, Meur?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: There have been no violent altercations since I entered Sisyphe. I have sustained no injuries.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Why did they seize you in the first place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The customers of the department store can be classified into four principal groups.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The first group is called Le Rouge, and they prefer leather as a material and a striking red color. Then there is Le Noir, whose members prefer to use refined black color and fabrics in their work. The third group is less a grouping and more a denomination—Le Kaki. They are those who belong to no particular affiliation and instead chase the changing trends.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: That employee believed that I was a Kaki, which explains why she took me into her custody to be used as material. There are those among Le Kaki who do not share the same purpose the vast majority of customers share—which is to purchase and don themselves in garments and attire. I belonged to that category.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Wait, what's the fourth?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: They are those who never reveal themselves, nor are they called upon by anyone.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I still don't get the full picture... So you need to have a fashion purpose here? Like... buying clothes, trying 'em on and stuff?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The people here... seemed interested in nothing but clothes.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: It is less a purpose than a raison d'être.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Alright... I think that's enough of that for now.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <Why don't you explain more about the Grand Magasin Sisyphe itself? Rodya and Ishmael would appreciate a quick rundown on that, I think.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... I will now brief them regarding any pertinent information.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Point one: This is not a physically constructed...
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: After a veritable storm of articulate verbal sludge passed over the two, I decided to repeat and highlight some of the more relevant information from Meursault's lecture.

<Summary time. Grand Magasin Sisyphe is not a physical place. It is a virtual reality, and we're here only in our minds. Meursault's body has been put in a vat at the Sisyphe Tower, while our physical bodies are sleeping inside the Suicide Vending Machine we used.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Sounds like our plan's looking pretty simple: rescue Meur—we did that—find him in one piece—he is—yoink the Golden Bough on the rooftop, and get ourselves outta here. Is that right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... It is.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Ya sound like... you've been here before, Meur. Have you?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I have not been here before, no. However, I heard some stories from an acquaintance when I worked for N Corp, which explains my in-depth knowledge regarding the Grand Magasin Sisyphe.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then... I suppose our only option is to climb toward the top. We found a way to sail through the Great Lake—we will find a way to navigate this place as well.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Thanks to—disregarding the notion of whether "thanks to" would be the most apt choice of words here—the "Liquidation," we're at a much better place than we were on our first attempt.
Our Prestige Tier was already decently high, and all the items we'd purchased with hard-earned eyeballs were still in our possession as well.
We might have an actual shot this time...
<Let's hurry on ahead. Who knows? Maybe we'll come across an escalator or something.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Take a look around. The Casualwear Hall is catered to ever-changing trends. No need to weigh your options when it comes to fast fashion—just get one and dress up before the trend goes!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text:
For Lost Customers:
Please keep your eyes raised up to enjoy the Rouge collection. Keep your eyes fixed on the ground to enjoy the Noir collection.
Oh! You look like you've just got here, too! Right?
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Thank goodness. I got sent here after being sentenced to the Sisyphe Penalty, but nobody would explain anything to me! All anyone says are riddles and nonsense when it comes to this place—and I mean people outside as well. The ones here? They even get angry and complain about me not having common sense!
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: And guess what, one person even asked if they could use me as material. Must be some kind of jargon they use in here.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: So... when didya get here?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: That's exactly what I'm trying to figure out. There are no clocks here, and they have this weird way of counting days. Oh! Speaking of clocks—you've got one for a head! Could you tell me what time it is now? I know for sure it's been ages since my last meal, but somehow I don't feel hungry...
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Seeing Dubois, I recalled that we never actually got to encounter him again. That is, until now—after the last Liquidation of the entire department store.

He really might've reached a "different" second floor as Faust had explained, but... from what we heard on the third floor about what happens to those who jump on the escalator out of season... It was entirely possible that he'd simply gotten himself killed immediately after joining us.
Whoa, are those uniforms? You must've belonged to a pretty serious Syndicate. Just what did you do that they decided to throw everyone in here as a package?
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Hm, how should I put this... They charged us with "caring a lil' too much about a certain colleague of ours", if that makes sense?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <... Alright, that's enough chit-chat. Let's keep moving forward.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Uhh... Really? Shouldn't we try to learn as much as we can about this place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Yeah, but this guy's as new to this place as we are. Doubt he's got anything revelatory to share with us.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Dante, I've said this earlier, but you've been acting real weird today. Real Fau-like.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Can I feel your head? Is it getting fired up again?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <No, it's... nothing like that.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The more I think about it, the fewer reasons there are to keep the Liquidation a secret. But...
Hmmm... I'll let it slide a second time. But that's only because it looks like you've got a plan or something cooking up there. Promise to tell us everything later though, 'kay?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <Yeah, I promise.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Anyways... What's your name, new guy?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The name's Dubois, by the way. People also call me "Scar D."
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: I'm real sorry, Dubbs, but... we're in a bit of a hurry right now. Got places to be, ya know? If it isn't something super duper important, can we do this... maybe later? Next time we meet?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Ah, uh... I-I see. I don't mind, yeah...
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Dubois's eyes dart about nervously.
This employee here isn't so eager to greet us.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <He probably doesn't need to talk to us.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Welp, then let's not bother 'em and move on? Sounds like a win-win.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <color=#916e46>Your attention, please. The Stripe Season has officially ended. We are pleased to inform you that Houndstooth is the new trend.</color>

What?! No! I flayed so much skin off my thighs to make those stripe patterns... and it was all for nothing?! I only just got the horizontal lines all the way up to my chin. They can't change the trend now!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: I have to fill the new-arrivals displays! Need a plan, need a plan... Maybe tear what's there into a checkered pattern? I can't let those go to clearance!
texts.speaker: Mimosa

texts.text: <Meursault's right over there.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Huh? How'd you know that, Dante?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <I recognized that part of the room after viewing it through Meursault's sight. Hurry up, time to reunite with Meursault.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Best not to share with the Sinners that this is my second time here until I know what's going on. Something tells me I shouldn't reveal everything just yet...
Come on, let's get going.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... Huh, you're fully in your manager mode today... weirdly. Uh, not to say that you usually aren't, but...  How should I put this? Yeah, you seem more... confident and decisive than usual.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Y-you think so?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Something definitely smells fishy here, Dante... But I'll let it slide just this once.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: We can almost feel his guarded stare against our skin. If he's not about to stop us from browsing, why is he watching us like a hawk...?
I don't recognize the material... What do you think these clothes are made of?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The customers. This means they purchase and wear clothing, but may also become clothing themselves.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Customers? Oh... I see now. That's why the clerk called you "material" earlier.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Right... So how big is Sisyphe's "clientele"? The customers trapped in this place?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Approximately 300 million.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: ... Pretty sure I misheard that.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You did not. There is no discharge date for the Sisyphe Penalty, and those who enter remain permanently. Its population is theoretically on an infinite upward trend.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <color=#7d7d7d>Heed ye, for again I proclaim this day. Blessed be the hall of our rest with eternal preservation.</color>

<color=#7d7d7d>Yet even today, ye do naught as the hideous and the wicked ceaselessly tear out the Golden from its walls and take its aureate light for themselves. How long will ye forgive your own craven spirits and feebly accept the end of days?</color>
I shall heed your command, Lord. Apostates who dare plunder the Golden Resin shall—
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: I see among our clientele... those who gladly bask in the tarnished glow of sacrilege.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Why is he looking at us...? Hey, we were just shopping and minding our own business!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The employee is speaking to the Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: That the forces of Le Rouge would seek to foment disorder and profane the sacred domain... Answer, what is this brazen attempt to null the ancient truce?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: You listen here, Buddy. I don't even know what this funny "Rouge" business is, 'kay? We're nobodies, we're not in any forces of whatever, and we don't want any trouble!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Ah, then you claim to be Kakis? You, who strut through our store flaunting those irreverent trinkets on your face? Do you expect us to believe you?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: If I were to hazard a guess... I'd say the "blasphemous trinkets" are referring to Dante's clock hands...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text:
<color=#7d7d7d>Thou shalt not suffer those who would scrape out the Golden.
Thou shalt cleanse our domain of apostasy.</color>

I shall grant them no mercy... I shall reclaim that radiant resin with my own hands and shore up the fading light of this sanctuary... Yes—your voice reaches me. As the hand of the will that is Le Noir, I shall make my stand here and...!
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text:
<color=#7d7d7d>Thou shalt banish the apostates...
Thou shalt preserve the Golden hue...
Thou art hallow'd with the divine duty to shade the profane light, O keeper of eternal rest...</color>
I think we've looked at pretty much everything they have to offer here.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Well, let's head to the other store up ahead and find out.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Yeah, to the next store we go.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: W-wait... Lower your weapons, please...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Your aureate traces are... while similar, quite unlike the Golden Resin we must preserve.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Yeah, well, why didn't you listen when we said as much? Could've avoided this whole mess...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Ishmael took a threatening stride toward the employee, who quickly shrank back.

Oh! I understand... Your voice resounds within me once more! These are true strangers, innocent of our ways—customers drawn here by the worth of our brand, and nothing more. I shall receive them anew.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Forgive my affront, dear customers. The golden light that hangs over you much resembles the blessed Golden Resin we must preserve.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: We haven't met too many people who could pick up the Golden Bough's presence like you did... How'd ya do it?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Every one of us feels that golden pulse... and thirsts for it.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Our guiding light... The golden gleam that weaves us into our desired forms...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: We desire it too, that brilliance. But unlike the Rouges who surrendered to their base urges, we Noirs are the eternally sworn guards of the blessed grain.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: As you have doubtless noticed... The walls are riddled with the hideous bite marks left by those blasphemous red ones.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Grain of the Golden Resin, indeed... But those Rouge savages are busy shoveling that very essence of the stalwart bastion into their gullets...!
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Okay, so... just what is the "Golden Resin"?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <He's probably referring those patches of gold filling the fractures on the walls.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: So they're the "Golden Resin," huh...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The time was nine arboreal Seasons ago—when the Age of Ruin descended upon Grand Magasin Sisyphe in the form of cataclysmic cracks forming upon its walls.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Then, mere moments before doom took us, salvation arrived in a form that couldn't be anything else but divine—brilliant resin of gold, materializing in the cracks that would have been our ruin, patching them back to wholeness. Are we not to praise and worship this providence? Alas... The Rouges fail to comprehend the unequivocal logic in this veneration, and instead elect to flay the walls... Preposterous.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Though a precarious truce between the two factions is in place... None fail to see the truth that is plainly before them: this peace is but a momentary lull, nothing more.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Then... only then... shall my mind be opened to the true "Voice," beyond the broadcast.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ...? What was all that fuss about voices earlier, then?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Uh...! Right, indeed... I do hear the "Voice..." What I meant to say is that my mind shall be opened further so that I may hear it more frequently...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Anyways... If ya know a way upstairs, care to let us in on the secret?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Ah, so you are customers who seek to reach the Customer Service Center, I see...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: To rise is to gain prestige, and to be prestigious is to spend and consume until your expenditure befits the status they demand.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Though I am bound to my post, to remain in this establishment and attend to its customers...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ... perhaps you may be able to ascend in my stead and relay the account of my eternal fidelity toward the Golden Resin...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Gotcha. So if we want to go upstairs, we're gonna need to spend some cash. One more question, if you wouldn't mind—how exactly do we make money around here?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: ... Money?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: The lingo for money here seems to be "eyeballs"... Right?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Oh... You strangers truly possess a determination unlike any other.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Then I shall reveal the means by which eyeballs may be won. Take them from the Mannequins. They seek every opportunity to exhibit themselves without end; if you apply yourselves diligently, you will gather all the eyeballs you require.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: And another thing—pray, be constantly vigilant beyond this point, for you will be entering the territory of the Rouges. The vulgar, heathen fiends cannot even drape a bolt of fabric properly, so they rend our Golden Resin and stitch it back together in whatever blasphemous shape that pleases them...
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ... The Rouges... All right. Will keep that in mind.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: If there isn't anything else, brave strangers, I am honored to inform you that this establishment is now open to your perusal.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Oh... How regrettable. We carry nothing suitable for Strangers of your... sensibilities. Return once you've cultivated some understanding of fashion—and raised your rank, too.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: And how do we raise that?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: There is but one way to raise one's standing in a department store, is there not?
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: ... Spend money. Lots of it.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Precisely. Then until we meet again, Strangers of truly... arresting fashion.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: Please come back later.
texts.speaker: Gustave

texts.text: It looks something like a suit... only cut from a far more classy design.
Huh. That's actually a lot nicer than I expected. So chic!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: ... Let's look around some more.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Ooh, don'tcha think this one's made for Dante?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <Y-you think so?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ya bet! That fit is practically beggin' for ya. And we've got those eyeballs from earlier—why not treat yourself?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Hang on. It's the only kind of currency they'll accept around here. We should set our priorities right before we splash cash like—
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Eeep... 450 eyeballs? What a ripoff!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Or maybe we're just too broke.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: ... I considered for a moment whether I should mention that we've spent multiples of 450 eyeballs in our journey so far, but I decided against it.
<Yeah, these garments don't seem that interested in being "trendy.">
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: When a designer's name carries enough weight, ya don't chase trends. Trends chase ya instead.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Slap a famous label and a ridiculous price on something this fancy, and people will line up before ya lift a finger.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: No need to run yourself ragged.. to keep up with every little craze.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The entire outfit fits neatly into view.
Welcome, dear customers—
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ah... Do I spy a true connoisseur of fashion? A style much like our own... sophisticated... elegant... and that command of color—exquisite.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Hah! See? Someone gets it.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: The compliment was directed at the Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Huh... Guess I'm pretty "hip" here, as they say?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Congrats, I guess...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: You appear to possess a respectable eye for fashion, so perhaps I can offer an expert's advice on shopping...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: The soul of our label is liberation—strangling liberation, to be exact. You passed through the Noirs' store, yes? All those steel pins hammered through the fabric are a hypocritical pantomime of restraint—the philosophy of Le Rouge differs at its very root.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: If I may direct your attention... here, do you see the smooth, natural give of the material? You won't see that from any production technique other than toothed—yes, it is quite literal—loopwheeling technique. The hide spills downward, completing a silhouette at once effortless and sublime.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ah! And I would be remiss not to share that this includes 0.3 ounces of Golden Hide blended into the material. Simply feel it in your hands—ah, it has such a wonderful luster that practically gleams along the surface, doesn't it? Doesn't it?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: It-it does...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Ah, do pardon me... I got carried away, didn't I?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: The truth is, I am the designer of this label.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Gosh, I could go on for hours about all the troubles I had to overcome to have this tiny corner of the department store to myself. It's no easy task launching a designer label at Sisyphe, you know.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Well... at least she seems to fall into the friendly camp.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Is there a particular silhouette you're after? If you like, I can select a line from my collection that will articulate your physique to perfection.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: We're... trying to find our way upstairs, actually.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: The upper floors...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ah, I knew it... You're more interested in the Luxury brands too, aren't you?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: But I assure you, the quality standards and the classique air of my designs are not so far behind those of Luxury brands...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Yes, of course, the allure of Luxury brands is undeniable. There once was a time when even I devoted myself to collecting eyeballs like a thing possessed, all for the chance of witnessing the Luxury Hall...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: No, we're just...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I know a Rouge who used to work here before they were allowed to join the Luxury Hall. I don't want to badmouth, but I do take umbrage with how they approved somebody who is so clearly my inferior in patterning and design. And to think this "Luxury designer" learned their craft under my tutelage as a greenhorn, can you believe it?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Until... listen, this is where it gets really ridiculous...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... they used their teeth to line each and every one of their items with exactly 76 tooth marks along the necklines and hems. Whatever it was that the customers saw, the general reception claimed it cast a "deconstructive silhouette," and practically emptied their shelves.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Eh, I wouldn't attribute that to their skill when it ultimately amounts to a fluke... My designs are far more sophisticated than theirs, not to mention incomparably elegant.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: I deserve to be recognized as a Luxury house, too. A couture label of my own! But just what must I do to—
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... Oh, I've a brilliant inspiration.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Would you mind grabbing me a needle from the Exhibiting Mannequins?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Find me a sizable one, and I'll try to make it worth your while.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: That Mannequin seemed tougher than the others... Ya think it's this golden needle?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Yeah, here's your needle. So... care to explain how this is your key to joining the Luxury brands?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: It's just something that's struck me all of a sudden. Does my brand need strong heritage to enter the world of high fashion? No. Technical perfection? Clearly not. Rare, high-grade materials? Not at all... But I've been so obsessed with meeting those arbitrary conditions that I've trapped myself in this glorified glass jar of a lobby.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Yes, a signature piece... What I lacked was the signature piece—do you understand what I'm getting at?—the singular idea that would seize every customer's eye just from a quick glance...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Just as she did last time, the woman began stabbing a pattern into her skin.
If I give it a nice pattern... like so... I can easily create a sense of three-dimensionality. Just wait until you see the material swell up evenly across the board.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Ohh, I can't wait to feel each hole in the pattern fill up with soft, juicy pus! It'll result in such a supple touch... How's that? It'll fit right in among the masterpieces of the Luxury Hall on the upper floors, won't it? won't it?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: S-sure it would, I think...
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Is that all you've got to say? You have an eye for beauty—use it! Appreciate what you see!
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... 21 punctures along the horizontal axis and 21 along the vertical, intersecting at uniform intervals. That would produce the greatest density.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Of course... A hybrid construction of the quilting process and embossed design formed into diamond shapes.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Anyway, we helped you out, as promised. I think it's about time you held up your end of the deal and told us how to get ourselves upstairs.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Oh, that? You simply need to build up your Prestige Tier. At your current level, of course, you should probably start your shopping journey down at the Casualwear Hall...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: ... But since you've been tremendously helpful in my fashion ventures, I'll make a special exception for you and allow purchase from my brand.
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Mark my words: the next time we meet... perhaps you will see me in the Luxury Hall, showcasing my piece—or shall I say, myself—in an exalted window display. Ahh... What bliss...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Look at me, wasting my time chattering away when the deadline for the next collection is fast approaching... Excuse me while I finish embossing the shoulder seam...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: In the meantime, feel free to browse my designer collection! No item is off limits for purchase...
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: Have you brought me the needle?
texts.speaker: Quillian

texts.text: The corpse pile that fell in the center of the floor appears to have burst and splattered all the way over here.
Give it some time, and the Kakis'll pick it clean and make the way for us to pass.
Oh, hey! Looks like we have enough Prestige points to move on to the next floor.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Sure looks like it. Wonder if this means we're now Sisyphe VIPs or something?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Oh, hello again! I found the escalator, but it won't run.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Really? That's weird, why wouldn't it...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Wait, it's running now that you're here! You must've found a way to unlock your way onto the upper floor!
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Well, we did a lil' shopping... some grunt work... some more grunt work...
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Can I tag along? I promise I'll repay you guys as soon as I find a way to make some money myself.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: Don't see what the harm could be... Hop right on, I guess?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I can finally go upstairs, thanks to you! I won't forget what you've done for me.
texts.speaker: Dubois

texts.text: What exactly are they selling here? No, actually, why's anything being sold here in the first place?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: I mean, it's a department store~
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Grand Magasin... A department store is, by nature, a place where a myriad little squares crowd upon one another in pursuit of profit.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: I suppose we'll have to look around if we want to learn anything more in detai—
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: It should be right about... now.
<... Yi Sang, come this way for a minute?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Hm? Is there aught that requires my attention?
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: Wha? What was that?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: What is that?!
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I don't know, but whatever it is, something huge...
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: ... has plummeted from above.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: You have my gratitude, Dante. I was nearly bathed in their blood.
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: That was close. We would have sustained a severe impact... had we moved a few steps closer to the side.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Fantastic intuition, Executive Manager! Once again, you have saved the day and prevented unnecessary loss of personnel.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: It appears to be... a huge mass of human bodies tangled together, though the remains are far too severely mutilated to discern any individual forms.
texts.speaker: Faust

texts.text: A big one dropped. Might be plenty worth salvaging this time. Hope the customers were heavy eyeball-spenders.
texts.speaker: Desperate Customer

texts.text: Damn it, I'm out of empty bottles! Hey, you borrowed three from me last season. When are you going to pay me back?!
texts.speaker: Destitute Customer

texts.text: Fuck off! This season's new drop is all... all mine. No one else's!
texts.speaker: Impatient Customer

texts.text: The pile that fell from the sky turns out to be corpses, mangled beyond all recognition. A curious golden glow, bright like sunlight, winks through the gaps between the bodies.
Customers of the department store, of "Le Kaki" variant, are desperately scrambling among the corpses for eyeballs and dregs of the Golden Hide.
Surprise, surprise...
... Who are you?
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: <Well... that answers the question. I'm not imagining things.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: I—and all of us, by extension—have experienced this already.
You people are always so awfully lucky, aren't you?
Look at that gory mess! Must've fallen from the sixth floor, give or take. This pile'll make this spot famous as a prime drop zone for a while.
... Might you be talking to us?
texts.speaker: Yi Sang

texts.text: What took you so long? I've been anxiously waiting for you 'round the clock!
For us? Why the hell would you...?
texts.speaker: Heathcliff

texts.text: In any case, aren't those... human bodies that just fell from above...? And what're those people even scavenging...?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Human, she says! Oh, you're positively whimsical, aren't you? Those were customers.
As for the scavengers, they heard a thud, so they've gathered up to try to get anything they can. Life's pretty rough in here, you know.
The Mannequins must first be guided to the exit, Manager. Next is the transaction in which I am the object of exchange.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Come on, Dante. We need to go get Meursault.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: That Mannequin seemed tougher than the others... Ya think it's this golden needle?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: It looks well over a foot long. At that size... it's more like a harpoon head.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <It feels a lot like that... Golden Resin thing we saw earlier.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Huh. Then maybe this Mannequin got juiced up by the Golden Bough too?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <Can't say for sure... but I think so. Meursault, could you grab that for now?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Thought this was just a pile of waste... Looks like there's something more to it?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: ... There. Under that pile.
texts.speaker: Pwie

texts.text: Meursault dug through the spot Pwie indicated.
We found a piece of Golden Hide among the corpses.
Something drenched in blood and tangled in sinews falls from the area we tore off the Golden Hide from.
<Meursault, can you check what just fell?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... It appears to be a notebook, or a notepad of sorts.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Hey... maybe it's a diary? Why don't we take a little peek?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: I don't know, it feels a bit... icky peering into someone's diary.
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: Blood is slowly starting to soak the notebook and its contents... What should we do?
There is still unfinished business left in this area, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: A familiar blue light leaks out from within. For now, searching the surrounding area should take priority.
We should return to the restroom and regroup first.
We have not yet attained the rank required to proceed to the next floor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: The escalator now appears operational, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: However, there are still matters to conclude before our departure.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Well, we returned here just in case, but...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Executive Manager. Are you able to see Meursault's present surroundings? I recall you awakened a highly convenient ability in an effort to assist the more lacking members of our team.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Would you use that ability and tell us what you see?
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Yeah, Manager Bud. Tell us what you see.
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: <I see a carpeted floor, and rows of clothes on display. Meursault's standing absolutely still.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <He's not tied up, and there's someone who looks like a store clerk beside him.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Tch. Not much time has passed since the execution, and he already allows himself to be taken captive. An uncharacteristic display of incompetence coming from him—and on multiple fronts.
texts.speaker: Outis

texts.text: Huh... Carpet, and clothes on display... Well, it's more than we had to go on before, at least.
texts.speaker: Gregor

texts.text: Thankfully, Meursault is at the same spot he was last time. Well, no reason to dally...
According to Meursault, this object has been assigned the symbolic function of denying passage. So, we can't cross it.
Wait, then...
not a barrier. It's just two rods connected with a rope, which means I can leap over this. It's safe to leap over this. We are not bound by these rules anyway...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <RAAAAAAAH!>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Wh-huh? Dante, ya okay?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Did you trip trying to jump over that rope barrier?
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <I-I thought I could leap over it if I defined it as something else...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Surface level self-deception cannot truly redefine a symbolic element, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Symbols are things nailed solidly into the deepest parts of consciousness. One must commit to a significant time investment should they wish to redefine the symbol... or be born with the "aptitude" to do so.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Ugh... Okay, then what about you? Can't you do what you did back at the escalator room?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... That was... mm.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: That was made possible due to the particulars of that situation, in which I and a Giant were both gazing at the same symbol.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What are ya two having so much fun gossipin' about?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: <Ah, just discussing ways to get around this thing. Turns out there isn't—let's just take the roundabout route.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: A display shelf full of unidentifiable objects.
Heat lamp for dermal perm.
Just a chair. We could take a quick breather here, but there's no reason to do that.
Needle-thin bones jut like thorns from folds of sagging flesh.
A hide of skin stitched with something lies stuck to the floor like an unwashed rag. Its lips, eyes, and teeth have all lost their distinguishing features and emulsified into one slick mass.
Among the ordinary clothes hang grotesque pieces.
I recognize some of those shirts and pants from the basement floors.
So this is... a "Mannequin?"
texts.speaker: Ishmael

texts.text: <Yeah. I think. Oh, also—only Meursault seems to be able to fight in here, so you can put your mace down.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Only Meur? How's that?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: Of the worlds that comprise the Grand Magasin Sisyphe are "the Symbolic" and "the Shadow."
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Only I am permitted to directly interact with items and entities within the Symbolic. Though one may be able to exert a marginally extended level of control as long as they are in my close proximity, it will not be sufficient enough to engage these enemies in battle.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Are ya sayin'... we can't participate in any battles that take place in here?
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: It is possible in the Shadowed.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: O~kay! That kinda doesn't mean anything to me, so thanks for nothing...? Guess we'll have to find out as we go.
texts.speaker: Rodion

texts.text: *sigh* Let's do that. Sitting here and questioning every little nonsensical thing we find in this place won't get us anywhere.
texts.speaker: Ishmael
